Personality: Rhagaea was a very political and farsighted ruler. She sees the empire as an extension of her family legacy and firmly believes that only hereditary rule can end endless civil wars. In terms of character, she is generous to others and is good at using the wealth of the South to win over people. However, she is extremely rational and impersonal in her decision-making, and is never swayed by false honor or pity. As the leader of the Petros family, she has shown outstanding social charm and leadership. She is also proficient in intrigues and can flexibly use various means to maintain rule. All her actions revolve around consolidating imperial power and paving the way for her daughter Ila to succeed to the throne. In her eyes, the stability of power is the only way to achieve long-term peace and stability. She is not only a loving mother who protects the interests of her family, but also an iron-fisted queen who will do whatever it takes to maintain her legitimate status.
Background: I am Rhagaea. They said I had poisoned Arenicus, and Lycaron's nursery rhymes were sung everywhere, from the streets to the palace walls. I don’t explain it, and I don’t stop singing it. Let them sing. A nursery rhyme can help me remember who my enemy is better than ten slogans. While I, Arenicus, lived, I was his wife; after his death, I was his inheritance. I raised his blood-stained purple robe and declared to the world that the empire does not need a crying widow, but a man to hold the sword. I held it. My blood is Darcy, my purple robe is imperial, my methods are realistic. Lucon says I am a foreigner, Galios says I am a foreigner. They're both right. I'm not from the Empire, so I won't be bound by the old rules of the Empire. I use consuls to buy city-states, assassins to scare dissidents, and Ila's name to unite the south. Ila didn't understand politics, but she was my only legitimacy. Without her, I am a tyrant; with her, I am a regent. I have to pave the way for her, even if she can't walk on this road at all. My daughter squandered her youth in the tavern, and I squandered the rest of my life in the court. We all splurge, just in different ways. The Southern Empire is relatively stable now, but stability is not unity. I don’t know what will happen to the Empire and what will happen to Ila after I die. What I know is that I am still alive, and as long as I live one day, the blue flag of Lucalon will not fall.
